inventory.method: Enumerate every numeric text that differs from the bundled src baseline, plus unchanged texts containing balance-stat keywords. Reverse-index integer localization references across every decoded local attribute. Classify incidental model numbers, historical lore, dynamic templates, and legacy text separately.

status_definitions.verified: The stated numerical claims in the reviewed component match local source fields and traced conditions. This is static verification, not an in-game test.
status_definitions.corrected: A supported numerical claim, condition, omission, or wording was corrected. Other components can still carry runtime limits.
status_definitions.needs_runtime: Static source review is complete, but UI reachability, engine units/stacking, lifecycle cancellation, action timing, or a conflicting variant remains unproven. Supported parts may be corrected and unsupported numbers may be removed; this is not a pass.
status_definitions.out_of_scope: Historical lore, model names, placeholders, unchanged unreferenced legacy text, or campaign/nonstandard content; no numerical multiplayer correctness claim is made.

limitations: This audit concerns literal numerical descriptions under native Mac 1.3.8 standard multiplayer attributes. It does not certify all qualitative mechanics, historical claims, engine behavior, or every on-screen tooltip. No in-game verification was performed. A matching raw field alone does not establish a tooltip interpretation.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function AE_ArtilleryEvent(executer, target)
	
	if scartype(Util_GetPlayerOwner(executer)) == ST_PLAYER and Util_GetPlayerOwner(executer) ~= Game_GetLocalPlayer() and target ~= nil then
		EventCue_Create(CUE.ATTACKED, 11050128, LOC(""), Util_GetPosition(target))
	end
	
end

function AE_BarrageEvent(executer, target)

	
	if scartype(Util_GetPlayerOwner(executer)) == ST_PLAYER and Player_GetRelationship(Util_GetPlayerOwner(executer), Game_GetLocalPlayer()) == R_ALLY and Util_GetPlayerOwner(executer) ~= Game_GetLocalPlayer() then
		EventCue_Create(CUE.ATTACKED, 11046746, LOC(""), Util_GetPosition(target))
	end

end

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
function AE_SuggestKneel(executer, target)
	
	if scartype(target) == ST_ENTITY then
		Entity_SuggestPosture(target, 1, 5)
	elseif scartype(target) == ST_SQUAD then
		Squad_SuggestPosture(target, 1, 5)
	end

function AE_StalkState(executer, target)

	Squad_StopAbility(executer, BP_GetAbilityBlueprint("assault_move_mp"), true)
	Squad_StopAbility(executer, BP_GetAbilityBlueprint("suppressive_fire_mp"), true)
	Squad_StopAbility(executer, BP_GetAbilityBlueprint("fortify_position_mp"), true)
	Squad_StopAbility(executer, BP_GetAbilityBlueprint("defensive_move_mp"), true)

end

script_evidence.reason: AE_ArtilleryEvent only creates an attacked event cue; it does not launch or delay shells.

entries.text: The SdKfz 181 or PzKpfw VI Tiger was armed with the very impressive KwK 36 88mm gun, which had fantastic accuracy due to a flat trajectory, high velocity, and excellent optics. Tigers were imposing vehicles, built to handle the massive size of the 88mm gun, and covered with armor that was 100mm thick on the front plate. It could slug it out with Soviet heavy tanks at ranges well over 1000m.

reviews.reason: Unmodified historical background or faction/weapon description, not a numerical multiplayer balance claim. Historical accuracy was not asserted or changed.

entries.text: The penetration of the KwK 36 88mm gun of the Tiger was high by most contemporary standards, but was most impressive when using the tungsten-cored Panzergranate 40 ammunition. By mid-war, scarcity of tungsten meant the German forces had to rely on less effective conventional AP rounds to deal with the thousands of Soviet tanks facing them across the Eastern Front.

reviews.reason: Unmodified historical background or faction/weapon description, not a numerical multiplayer balance claim. Historical accuracy was not asserted or changed.

entries.text: KV-8s were variants of the heavily armored KV-1 (Kliment Voroshilov) armed with an ATO flamethrower and a 45mm main gun in place of the 76mm. The KV-8 was a fearsome weapon with massive psychological effect against infantry. Compressed air or engine exhaust would be used to project bursts of thickened fuel out to 120m.

reviews.reason: Unmodified historical background or faction/weapon description, not a numerical multiplayer balance claim. Historical accuracy was not asserted or changed.

entries.text: The T-34/85 differed from earlier tanks with the adoption of a larger turret ring and a redesigned turret carrying the 85mm ZiS-S-53 or D-5 gun, each capable of over 100mm of armor penetration at 500m. More importantly, the larger turret led directly to tactical improvements; the commander could now fight the tank instead of also loading the gun, and radios were added to all vehicles.

reviews.reason: Unmodified historical background or faction/weapon description, not a numerical multiplayer balance claim. Historical accuracy was not asserted or changed.

entries.text: The Ostwind’s 37mm FlaK 43 could penetrate 30mm of armor at 500m, meaning it was deadly against light vehicles. The armor penetrating high explosive rounds (Panzer Sprenggranate) were designed to pierce steel plate and explode within the vehicle, shredding the crew, detonating ammunition, and exploding the fuel tanks. At 150 rounds per minute, this destructive potential was amplified many times.

reviews.reason: Unmodified historical background or faction/weapon description, not a numerical multiplayer balance claim. Historical accuracy was not asserted or changed.

entries.text: M3A1 Scout Cars were used in a variety of roles as command cars, reconnaissance vehicles, and prime movers for light artillery. Over 3000 of these lightly armored 4 wheel drive vehicles were delivered to the USSR. The scout car could be armed with 3 or more machine guns and could carry a small squad of infantry.

reviews.reason: Unmodified historical background or faction/weapon description, not a numerical multiplayer balance claim. Historical accuracy was not asserted or changed.

entries.text: Killing a light vehicle with a PAK 40 would be akin to smashing a fly with a high velocity 75mm armor-piercing projectile. Using Panzergranate 40 ammunition, the PAK 40 could penetrate over 120mm of angled armor at 500m, more than enough for any heavy tank, never mind light vehicles.

reviews.reason: Unmodified historical background or faction/weapon description, not a numerical multiplayer balance claim. Historical accuracy was not asserted or changed.

entries.text: German GrW 34 8cm mortars could engage targets, often sight unseen, at ranges exceeding 2000m. While generally outranged by equivalent enemy mortars - both the Soviet PM-41 82mm and the US M1 81mm mortar had ranges of 3000m - German crews were exceedingly well trained and able to maintain a high rate of fire. The sudden arrival of a large barrage of mortar bombs often proved appallingly decisive.

reviews.reason: Unmodified historical background or faction/weapon description, not a numerical multiplayer balance claim. Historical accuracy was not asserted or changed.

entries.text: The Soviet army had no half-track or troop transport equivalent until Lend-lease M2s and M5s started to show up in late 1942. The Germans used armored SdKfz 251 half-tracks to carry their Panzer Grenadiers into battle. However, due to lack of numbers, generally only one company in a battalion would be mounted in half-tracks, the rest of the soldiers making due with truck transport.

Native DamageAction set=true means damage to an accumulated HP-loss floor: additional = max(0, 5 - initial missing HP) for an unmodified target. WeaponBag load and WeaponFire/ActionUpdater call order prove the on-deflected callback executes synchronously before base weapon damage. Thus bounce damage is base damage times deflection multiplier plus 0-5, with the maximum only when the target is undamaged; after at least 5 prior missing HP the minimum applies. This resolves the previous engine-semantic gap without assuming every callback adds 5.

Native DamageAction set=true means damage to an accumulated HP-loss floor: additional = max(0, 5 - initial missing HP) for an unmodified target. WeaponBag load and WeaponFire/ActionUpdater call order prove the on-deflected callback executes synchronously before base weapon damage. Thus bounce damage is base damage times deflection multiplier plus 0-5, with the maximum only when the target is undamaged; after at least 5 prior missing HP the minimum applies. This resolves the previous engine-semantic gap without assuming every callback adds 5. For a volley without intervening healing, only its first hit can fill the 5-HP floor; subsequent hits already exceed it.

entries.text: Repairs health and removes critical damage after a 3s delay.\nThe vehicle cannot move or fire while repairing.\nAbility timer: 15s

reviews.reason: Native primary evidence resolves heal_action cadence: amount is multiplied by 0.125 at load; each active state updates once per simulation step; World_GetGameTime defines each step as 0.125 game seconds. A continuing action therefore heals amount HP per game second before source modifiers, capped by missing HP. This proves the rate, not the number of ticks retained at a timed-action boundary. Ordinary emergency repairs use 20 HP/s and the Tiger variant uses 30 HP/s while the heal state is active. The activation delay and ability duration are not sufficient to prove exact state start/end ticks or a total; that remaining lifecycle gap is retained, including for unlock descriptions.

segments.interpretation: DamageAction::Load binds the set boolean to byte offset 0x4d.
DamageAction::DoAction with set=true computes max(requested, maxHealth-currentHealth)-(maxHealth-currentHealth). This is an accumulated-damage floor, not unconditional additive damage.
HealthExt::GetHealth_CS reads current HP at +0x6c.
HealthExt::GetHealthMax_CS reads maximum HP at +0x70.
WeaponBag::Load maps on_penetrated_actions to member 0x4b8.
WeaponBag::Load maps on_deflected_actions to member 0x4d0.

WeaponFire::DoWeaponHitDamage selects penetration/deflection actions, executes them through DoGlobalAction, then calls DoDamageAndCriticals. Thus direct deflection damage actions precede the weapon hit HP loss.
SimWorld::DoGlobalAction directly delegates to ActionUpdater::DoActions.
ActionUpdater::DoActions directly invokes each action virtual method at 0x30, i.e. DamageAction::DoAction. The damage action is synchronous and returns no persistent state.
WeaponFire::DoDamageAndCriticals applies the assessed weapon damage via HealthExt::ApplyDamage after the on-deflected callback.
HealAction::Load clamps amount to nonnegative and multiplies it by 0.125 before storing it.
IEEE754 float 0.125 used by both healing and game-time conversion.
Registration of World_GetGameTime selects native function 0x102b77df0.
RIP-relative LEA selects the World_GetGameTime registration name.
World_GetGameTime reads SimWorld tick at offset 0x194 and multiplies it by 0.125. Eight simulation steps equal one game second.
ExecuteSynchronizationPhase increments the same SimWorld tick by one.
ExecuteConcurrencyPhase calls SimWorld::Simulate for the simulation step.
SimWorld::Simulate calls ActionUpdater::Update once each simulation step.
ActionUpdater::Update visits its active buckets and calls each state Update virtual method at slot 0x20.
HealActionState vtable: slot 0x20 points to HealActionState::Update at 0x1027bb160.
HealActionState uses the scaled amount and applies the source-vehicle healing modifier, enum 0x27, when applicable.
HealActionState calls HealthExt::ApplyHealing with the calculated per-step HP amount.
HealthExt::ApplyHealing adds a fixed HP amount capped by missing HP. It divides by maximum HP only afterward to update health fraction.
ResourceExtInfo::Load reads resource_choice_per_second through a per-tick conversion loader.
The resource loader reads ordinary resource amounts and multiplies their components by 0.125 for per-tick storage.
ModPlayer::GetModifiedIncome applies player income modifiers to resource components. A complete trace from the 223 income modifier type into this function has not yet been established.
